title: The Counter-Offer
prompt:
Korean drama scene, 15 seconds, live-action, cinematic, soft contrast, warm skin tones, teal shadows. A hushed upscale hotel lounge in Seoul in the afternoon, tall windows with soft daylight, a white marble table with two white teacups.

Characters (keep identical throughout): on the left, an elegant woman in her late fifties with a silver-streaked low bun, cream tweed jacket and pearl necklace; on the right, a woman in her late twenties with long straight black hair tucked behind her ears, olive-green knit cardigan over a white T-shirt, small gold hoop earrings.

0–4s: Medium two-shot at table height, slow push-in. The older woman slides a thin white envelope across the marble with two fingers and says in Korean, slow and cold, in a deep voice: "이거 받고 내 아들한테서 떨어져." Soft lounge ambience, the envelope scrapes on marble.
4–7s: Close-up of the young woman, static. She looks down at the envelope, then up, and slowly smiles. She lifts a much thicker brown envelope from her lap and places it on the table with a heavy thud. A low cello drone stops into silence.
7–11s: Over-the-shoulder shot from behind the older woman. The young woman slides the brown envelope across, leans in, and says in Korean, calm and sweet, in a clear younger voice: "이걸로 아드님 저 주세요."
11–15s: Close-up of the older woman, slow push-in. Her teacup stops halfway to her lips, her eyes widen, she glances down at the brown envelope and back up, and says quietly in Korean: "얼마 들었니?" The teacup rattles on its saucer, a single bright plucked note and a light comic piano sting.

Natural Korean voices, clear lip sync, two clearly different voices. No subtitles, no text, no watermark.
